lede:
All thirty-six cut, and you are right that tweaking nouns is not working. So before writing another prompt I laid out every illustration that has ever been accepted — all eleven — and looked at them as a set for the first time.

Nine of eleven are the same kind of picture, and it is not the kind I have been asking for

They are wide exterior shots in the void. A dark starfield or nebula ground, one bright warm event, hardware seen in profile, and depth behind it — a planet, a station, a target. The two that are not (range_card, cold_read) are flat instrument faces, a scope and a screen. That is the entire vocabulary.

Not one of them is an interior. No compartments, no deck grating, no conduit, no lit viewport seen from inside, no people. And full_auto — the belt and the brass — is the single odd one out, which is exactly the one you looked at before saying the art should be spaceship and space opera themed.

So my last three rounds were built on a rule I invented: put the camera inside a ship and give it a viewport. The design doc paragraph I took it from is about how SHIPS and STATIONS look in the world view, not about what a card shows. Every brief below moves the camera outside.

Two of my own rules also turn out to be wrong and are dropped: “no gun in frame” — siege_round, suppressing_fire and cutting_beam are all hardware firing, and all three are accepted. And “never a muzzle flash”, which four of the eleven have. The problem was never the gun. It was the room.

cards.actor: a cutting arc reaching out from the frame edge
cards.on: a dead wreck drifting in the void
cards.moment: the arc has been at it a while: a long slot glowing white at the tip and cooling to red and then to black along the wreck's flank, slag beads drifting off into vacuum because there is no down. The wreck is dark, tumbling slightly, unlit. Wide shot, the whole thing in frame, nebula behind.
cards.scale: the wreck reads large because the cut is small against it and the debris around it is smaller still. Nothing is close to the camera.
cards.world: exterior, in the void — the same camera as cutting_beam and siege_round. Dark starfield with a rusty amber nebula wash, everything coldly lit, the arc the only warm light in frame.
cards.avoid: any interior. No compartment, no deck, no grating, no conduit, no figure, no viewport seen from inside — nine of eleven accepted illustrations are exteriors and every interior round has been cut. Do not say hull, vessel, derelict, shell or starship.

cards.actor: a row of hits walking along a target
cards.on: another craft's flank, seen from outside at a distance
cards.moment: the walk read across the whole target rather than close on plating: a line of flashes marching down its side, the leading hit bright and throwing debris, the ones behind it fading to smoke and scars. The target is intact enough to still be a target. A planet or station gives the depth behind.
cards.scale: the target sits mid-frame at a distance, small enough that the whole line of hits fits across it. That distance is what makes it a fight rather than a texture.
cards.world: exterior, in the void — the camera of suppressing_fire, which is accepted. Cold light everywhere, the impacts the only warm source, nebula wash behind.
cards.avoid: the close-up on plating I have now tried twice: rivets, craters and stencils fill the frame with texture and no event. No interior, no figure. Do not say hull, vessel, shell or starship.

cards.actor: an ordnance rack on the outside of a spine
cards.on: a fresh canister sliding into the empty slot
cards.moment: seen from outside along the spine: a row of loaded canisters, one gap, and a fresh canister on a rail being pushed home into it. Nothing is firing. The card is the reload, and the empty slot filling is the whole story.
cards.scale: the spine runs out of frame and the canisters are regular along it, so the count reads at a glance and the machinery reads as big.
cards.world: exterior, in the void. Cold light with one warm indicator lamp on the rack, stars and nebula behind the spine.
cards.avoid: the magazine interior, which failed twelve times. Also never say ROUND for the thing being loaded — nine of twelve takes drew a literal sphere hanging on a chain. Say canister, cartridge or projectile. Do not say hull, vessel, shell or starship.
